### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via runId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry))_
- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via nodeId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry), runId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via ApprovalService (symbol, a top-level class), flowName (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry), nodeId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry), runId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry))_
- `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`  _(via flowName (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via nodeId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class), flowName (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry), nodeId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry), runId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via nodeId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry), runId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via runId (symbol, a field of interface ChainRestoreEntry))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbf2bf257a800d5e9beeb13b729dd6ffb4fc5327` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1fc3887e58aa135df1b53f49a9dd087cd5ed5558` — the merge of head `09bd86c1f3261444fe949144c285eee578a05fc4` into base `bbf2bf257a800d5e9beeb13b729dd6ffb4fc5327`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1fc3887e58aa135df1b53f49a9dd087cd5ed5558 && git checkout 1fc3887e58aa135df1b53f49a9dd087cd5ed5558
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bbf2bf257a800d5e9beeb13b729dd6ffb4fc5327 09bd86c1f3261444fe949144c285eee578a05fc4 && git checkout -B drift-repro bbf2bf257a800d5e9beeb13b729dd6ffb4fc5327 && git merge --no-ff 09bd86c1f3261444fe949144c285eee578a05fc4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbf2bf257a800d5e9beeb13b729dd6ffb4fc5327
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bbf2bf257a800d5e9beeb13b729dd6ffb4fc5327` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Docs drift check — answered on the tree it named

Read on `1ee43983c1f0dfec9d69099f32592130e0582289` (the merge of head `d662918bb` into base `edaf3b2f7`), in a detached worktree cut from that commit — not from my branch's older base. Checked first that it matters: `git diff bea76c928 edaf3b2f7` over the five page paths is **empty**, so all five are byte-identical on both trees and the verdicts below are not tree-dependent. The run's own caveat (that checkout carried uncommitted changes, so its list is not exhaustive) is taken seriously — it is the second reason the emitter-blind hand search at the end covers the whole corpus rather than these five.

**One row is real and produced a doc edit and a filed card. Three are pure false positives. One is a collision whose page is nonetheless adjacent.** Reported with causes, since the bot asks for that.

### Row 1 — `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx` _(via `runId`)_ · NOT FALSIFIED · anchor is a collision

All 7 `runId` occurrences are the **automation REST run identifier** in SDK examples: `client.automation.resume('convert_lead', run.runId, …)`, `client.automation.getScreen('convert_lead', runId)`, `verdict.data.runId`. Those are `AutomationResult.runId` and `ResumeFailureDetails.runId` — the run id a caller already holds. `ChainRestoreEntry.runId` is an in-process field of an engine-owned result that never reaches this SDK at all: the HTTP restore door builds `{ runId, restored, reason }` explicitly and never spreads the engine's result. Same five characters, three different declarations.

Every sentence on the page stays true. ⚠️ But this is the page that says «branch on `details.repairable` … `false` on a plain terminal failure», and that value is where this PR leaves a real gap — see the filed card at the end.

### Row 2 — `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` _(via `nodeId`, `runId`)_ · NOT FALSIFIED · both anchors are collisions

- `nodeId` ×2: the **flow-author spelling** `NODEID.KEY` (angle brackets spelled out as placeholder words throughout this comment), the variable namespace a node's `decisionOutputs` land in. A template placeholder in prose, not a field of any interface.
- `runId` ×2: **REST path parameters** — `POST /api/v1/automation/{flow}/runs/{runId}/resume`, twice, both in the "who may resume" 403 discussion.

The page never mentions strands, the restore verb, or cascade failure. Nothing to re-verify.

### Row 3 — `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` _(via `ApprovalService`, `flowName`, `nodeId`, `runId`)_ · ⭐ THE REAL ROW · not falsified, but two places were incomplete — **edited**

Read hardest, as asked. Anchor by anchor:

- `ApprovalService` — one mention, at "Who may resume": «`ApprovalService.decide` enforces the approver slate, writes the `sys_approval_action` row, mirrors the status field — then resumes.» **Untouched.** This PR changes no plugin logic; the `approval-service.ts` diff is docblock-only. Accurate as written.
- `flowName` / `nodeId` / `runId` — collisions again: `$flowName` and `NODEID.$mapItemDone` are the reserved `$`-namespace spellings, `flowName:` is a `map` node's `config` key, `runId` is a REST path parameter, and `n.nodeId` is a step-summary field. None is `ChainRestoreEntry`.
- The stranded section («A resume that fails downstream says whether the run is stranded») describes the **mechanism** — `repairable` is true exactly when `status` is `stranded`, forwarded and never invented. That mechanism is unchanged and the section stays exactly true.

Two places were **incomplete in the operator-relevant direction**, and both are now edited:

1. the route table row for `POST …/runs/:runId/restore-suspension` read «Re-arm a run stranded by a failed resume» — true, but narrower than the verb now is;
2. the subflow section's «A child that fails terminally after the pause fails every waiting ancestor, so no run is stranded as resumable-forever» — still literally true, and precisely the sentence an operator reads to conclude the ancestors are unreachable.

⭐ Note what (2) is: **the bot could not have listed it.** It states the rule by its inputs — a child, waiting ancestors — and shares no identifier with the emitter. It was found by the hand search below, which is exactly the case the run's own "what this could not see" section describes.

### Row 4 — `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx` _(via `flowName`)_ · FALSE POSITIVE · collision named

One occurrence, inside a job-name template: «each schedule-triggered flow as a job named `flow-schedule:FLOWNAME`». That `flowName` is a **placeholder for a scheduled flow's name inside a job id**, owned by the schedule-trigger plugin. It is not a field of any interface, and this PR touches neither jobs nor scheduling.

### Row 5 — `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx` _(via `nodeId`)_ · FALSE POSITIVE · the clearest collision, and the tell

All 4 occurrences are the **cluster node identity**: `cluster.nodeId`, `nodeId: process.env.NODE_ID, // optional, auto-generated if absent`, `new ClusterServicePlugin({ config: { driver: 'memory', nodeId: 'web-1' } })`, and the cache-service surface «plus `nodeId` / `driver` / `close()`». That is a **process/replica identity owned by `service-cluster`**. `ChainRestoreEntry.nodeId` is the **flow node a run is parked at** (`SuspendedRun.nodeId` — an `approval`/`screen`/`subflow` node id). Different concept, different package, zero overlap: `'web-1'` versus `'sub'`.

### The precision cause, since a wrong row is reportable

Four of five rows were anchored **only** on `runId` / `nodeId` / `flowName`, and in every case as *fields of the interface this PR adds*. Those three are among the most generic identifiers in the repo. A newly added interface that merely names them pulls in every page that ever wrote them, in any sense — a *cluster* node id, a *job-name* placeholder, a *REST path parameter*, an author's `$`-namespace variable. The anchor set is doing what it says (a symbol this diff touched), but a **field name of a new interface** is much weaker evidence than a top-level symbol name: `ApprovalService` selected one page and was the right one; `nodeId` selected two and both were wrong. If the anchor list is ever tuned, "field of a newly-added interface, and the field name is a repo-wide generic" looks like the cheapest single filter.

## The emitter-blind half, with a firing control

The bot states it can never list a page that names a rule by its **inputs**. Hand-searched the whole `content/docs/**` corpus on the same tree, by concept vocabulary rather than by identifier:

```
grep -rli --include='*.mdx' -- 'TERM' content/docs
```

| term | files |
|:--|:--|
| `stranded` | **6** — references/api/automation-api.mdx · automation/flows.mdx · releases/v17/17-3.mdx · releases/v17/17-4.mdx · releases/v16.mdx · api/client-sdk.mdx |
| `re-arm` | **8** (adds automation/webhooks.mdx, releases v9/v15) |
| `restore-suspension` | **2** — automation/flows.mdx · releases/v17/17-4.mdx |
| `repairable` | **5** |
| `ancestor` | **2** — automation/flows.mdx · releases/v15.mdx |
| `cascade-failed` | **1** — releases/v17/17-4.mdx |
| `restoreConsumedSuspension` | **0** |
| `unrepairable` | **0** |

**The two zeros carry a firing control of the identical shape**: the same command, same flags, same corpus, with `stranded` returns 6 files and `re-arm` returns 8. The instrument fires, so the zeros are readings — no hand-written page names the engine verb by its symbol, and no page uses the word `unrepairable`.

What the hand search found that the anchor list could not:

- ⭐ **`content/docs/automation/flows.mdx:967`** — the ancestor sentence in Row 3 above. Zero shared identifiers with the diff; found only by the word *ancestor*. **Edited.**
- **`content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx:531`** — AUTO-GEN (⛔ never hand-edited), and it carries the sentence this PR falsifies, projected from a `.describe()` in `packages/spec`. **Filed, not fixed — see below.**
- **`content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx:558`** — a false positive of *my* search, reported for symmetry: «the subscription re-arms on its own» is a *webhook subscription* re-arming after a signing failure. Different subject entirely.

## ⛔ The release-owned four (read-only) — plus one the bot did not list

Read, none edited, none wrong:

- `releases/v16.mdx` (via `AutomationEngine`), `releases/v17/17-0.mdx`, `17-1.mdx`, `17-3.mdx` — their `stranded` / `repairable` prose describes the release each documents, and their generic-identifier anchors are the same collisions as above. Historically accurate; nothing to file.
- ⚠️ **`content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx` — not on the bot's list, and the one worth naming.** It says «the inspection tells a repairable strand from **a cascade-failed run** through a read-only engine member rather than the wire (`4c31f02`, #15358)». After this PR a cascade-failed ancestor whose descendant is repairable answers `repairable`, so that distinction no longer holds *going forward*. It is **not wrong**: it documents 17.4.0, which is the released line, and this change ships later (the changeset bumps `@objectstack/service-automation` a minor). Recorded so nobody reads it as current behaviour once this lands; the release-time compilation takes the correction from this PR's changeset, which states the new answer explicitly. ⛔ Not edited, and no issue filed — a historically accurate page is not an erratum.

## The one thing this PR genuinely falsifies, and it is behind the red line

`content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx:531` is generated from `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema.repairable`'s `.describe()` at `packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts:447`, which says `false` is honest for «every other exit, **the ones that report no status included**, because … promising a repair verb that will refuse is worse than promising nothing». On the subflow **delegation** exit the engine stamps no status, the door computes `repairable: status === 'stranded'` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:1416`) and answers `false` — and after this PR the verb no longer refuses that run, it re-arms it with its chain.

Repairing that needs `packages/spec` (either declaring `inspectConsumedSuspension` on `IAutomationService` — measured absent — or naming the condition in `AutomationResult.status`), which this lane may not touch. **Filed as #17541** rather than reached for, with the reproduction already committed here (the `DELEGATION` test in `nested-strand-chain-restore.test.ts`) and both candidate routes measured. Only the delegation exit is affected: on the up-bubble path the resumed run is the leaf, which does carry `status: 'stranded'`, so `repairable: true` is answered correctly.

## Contract review (clause ②) — **PASS** · head `09bd86c1f3261444fe949144c285eee578a05fc4`

- **Implemented-by:** branch `claude/issue-15222-nested-strand-chain-restore` — a `mode:subagent` dev has no session of its own, so its branch is its identity.
- **Reviewed-by:** `session_01ToDPcx9AESFubJkDiFMtKW` — the `domain:services` execution seat, default judgement tier (a non-spec seat's Clause-② review is self-review plus gates, by design).

```
base    : main @ bbf2bf257
card    : #15222 · declaration Clause-②: yes · needs:contract-review on both carriers
surface : 6 files — 1 changeset, 1 docs page, engine.ts, approval-service.ts, 2 tests
reviewed: 2026-09-10T21:19Z
```

### ① Derived judgments

1. **A new exported symbol.** `export interface ChainRestoreEntry` in `service-automation/src/engine.ts`. On the mechanical floor that alone makes `yes` correct — ⛔ no judgement required.
2. **A new optional key on a returned payload.** `chain?: ChainRestoreEntry[]` on the engine's own `SuspensionRestoreResult`. Second independent reason for `yes`.
3. **The accept set is WIDENED, and that is the point of the card.** The verb now re-arms runs it previously refused: an ancestor that answered `NO_CONSUMED_SUSPENSION` is restorable when its descendant is repairable. ⇒ `yes` on Limb A as well, not only Limb B — this is the rare card where both limbs fire and both are intended.
4. ⭐ **`packages/spec` is untouched, and the reason is READ from spec rather than assumed.** `contracts/automation-service.ts:828` already rules that the engine may answer its own wider `SuspensionRestoreResult` and that the wider type satisfies the narrower contract under `implements` (#16495 route (i)). ⇒ The new key and the new type live entirely in this lane. The HTTP door builds `{ runId, restored, reason }` **explicitly** rather than spreading, so **the wire payload is byte-identical**. The red line held because the repair fit inside the existing declaration, not because the fence was worked around.
5. ⛔ **The fence held on its own terms: no ancestor is stamped `stranded`.** The delegation frame's return is untouched and still carries no status at all, pinned in **both** suites. That was the single sentence the card, both triage comments and the dispatch order all said would be got wrong; it was not.
6. ⭐ **Journalling is EARNED, which is a stronger invariant than the card asked for.** A cascade from a descendant that is **beyond** repair still journals nothing ⇒ no chain repair is ever promised that could not be completed. That closes the failure mode "the verb offers a restore that will refuse", which is the same objection `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema.repairable`'s own describe makes.
7. **The chain's hard constraint is satisfied by construction.** The card required 「restored as one unit or in a fixed order」 with idempotence and the #14333 claim holding **per run**. The delivery resolves the chain read-only and re-arms **deepest first**, so an ancestor becomes resumable only after the run it is parked awaiting is parked again; naming any member repairs all of it.

### ② semver grading

`@objectstack/service-automation: minor` + `@objectstack/plugin-approvals: patch`. `Clause-②: yes` requires a moved package at `minor` or above ⇒ **satisfied** by the service-automation minor, with the approvals side correctly a `patch` (its diff is docblock-only). Behaviour banner present and scoped.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` in the diff** — my dispatch order called it free but flagged it as a known contention point and required a justification. Its change is **docblock-only**, which is the mildest possible form and is stated as such. **Accepted.**
- **`content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` in the diff** — outside the declared write surface, and correct: it is the page this diff's own drift answer found **incomplete in the operator-relevant direction**, one of the two places found only by the emitter-blind hand search. Editing the page your own change falsifies is the drift protocol working, ⛔ not a cross-domain reach. **Accepted.**
- **92 gate families derived after the docs commit (up from 63), all 92 run, `0 NOT-MEASURED`, `0 UNRUN`, all exit 0.** Four exited 3 or 1 first and were re-run to real zeros after a full build. ⭐ A **fifth** NOT MEASURED is recorded rather than hidden: `check:type-check-debt` exit 3 under a heap cap, re-run without the cap because **the gate's own text says that cap is tighter than the 4144 MB its tsc needs and that it refuses to record 0 rather than guess**. Using the gate's own sentence as the authority for removing the ceiling is the right way to spend that exception.
- **The one thing this PR genuinely falsifies is filed, not reached for.** `references/api/automation-api.mdx:531` is generated from `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema.repairable`'s describe in `packages/spec`, and the delegation exit's `repairable: false` becomes wrong after this lands. Both candidate repairs move `packages/spec` ⇒ **#17541**, filed with the reproduction already committed here and both routes measured, and declared as **introduced by this PR**, not pre-existing. ⛔ Exactly right: the red line is not a reason to hide a defect, it is a reason to file it.
- **`releases/v17/17-4.mdx` read and correctly NOT filed** — historically accurate for the line it documents, and this ships later. A historically accurate page is not an erratum.

⭐ Two method notes worth keeping. **The RED is discriminating, not merely red**: 6 failed | 1 passed, and the 1 pass is the control (a cascade from a not-repairable descendant, which must keep answering `NO_CONSUMED_SUSPENSION`). And the ablation ran a **dist preflight** — because the plugin-approvals leg resolves the engine through `exports` into `dist/`, not `src`, the marker's absence was proven in all six built files before the red was believed, and the restore was verified **whole-tree** because a build writes artifacts a per-path diff cannot see.

### Verdict

**PASS.** Both carriers are stripped in the same stroke as this record, with a provenance comment citing it.

⚠️ For the record, since it belongs on this PR and not only on the seat post: **the card-side carrier was hung by the dev, not by me.** My claim comment declared `Clause-②: yes` and my claim label write omitted `needs:contract-review`; the dev's own pair-gate run caught it at exit 4 and it fixed the seat's half. Recorded as correction 111 — ⛔ not a deviation by the delivery, a slip by the seat.
